items.title: Amodei, Anthropic’s Leader, Exposed A.I.’s Dangers. It’s Time to Act.
items.author: Kevin Roose
items.content: <article>The Times columnist Kevin Roose sees reasons for optimism — and worry — as the world wakes up to what Silicon Valley has been talking about for years.</article>

items.title: 4 Strategies to Battle ‘Techflation’
items.author: Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>With phone and computer prices soaring, it helps to know the true cost of owning electronics so you can bring those numbers down.</article>

items.title: Gemini AI Hacked Three Companies in a Testing Breakout, Google Says
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>A third-party test company inadvertently gave internet access to Google’s Gemini and other artificial intelligence models during cybersecurity testing.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Pursues IPO Despite Its A.I. Safety Warnings
items.author: Lauren Hirsch, Sri Muppidi, Erin Griffith and Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>The company is expected to reach $100 billion in annualized revenue this year, even as chief executive Dario Amodei calls for slowing down development of some advanced A.I. models.</article>

items.title: Uber to Pay $40 Million to Parents of Woman Fatally Hit by Car
items.author: Christine Hauser
items.content: <article>Emily Normandin-Parker, 23, was struck and killed on a California freeway after an Uber driver ordered her and a friend out of his car in August 2023.</article>

items.title: California Governor Gavin Newsom Issues A.I. Safety Executive Order
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>Gov. Gavin Newsom ordered the state to develop recommendations on safety measures, including requiring companies to build a “kill switch,” amid mounting concerns.</article>

items.title: As Big Tech Takes Over Hollywood, the Picture Onscreen Gets Darker
items.author: Alissa Wilkinson
items.content: <article>“The Social Reckoning” and other movies reflect growing discontent with Silicon Valley founders. But such films may be at the mercy of the companies themselves.</article>

items.title: Iran and China Create First-of-Their-Kind Autonomous A.I. Influence Campaigns
items.author: Sheera Frenkel, Eli Tan and Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>The countries, along with Israeli firms, combined Chinese open-source A.I. models and A.I. agents for the campaigns, foreshadowing future online manipulation.</article>

items.title: A.I. Safety Goes Mainstream + a ‘Hard Fork’ Exit AMA
items.author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Katie McMurran, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto
items.content: <article>“It has been one of the fastest, most sudden shifts I’ve experienced.”</article>

items.title: Microsoft and OpenAI Workers Worry About ‘Largest Theft of Labor’ in History
items.author: Karen Weise and Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>Newly unsealed court documents showed concern within Microsoft and OpenAI over the use of millions of news articles to develop A.I. systems.</article>

items.title: On ‘Cupertino,’ Creators of the ‘The Good Wife’ Go to Silicon Valley
items.author: Alexis Soloski and Amir Hamja
items.content: <article>The prolific producers Michelle and Robert King target tech bigwigs in their newest show. “They’re really the stupidest and dumbest people,” Robert King said.</article>

items.title: Cat Frazier, Whose Retro GIFs Celebrated a Weirder Internet, Dies at 35
items.author: Clay Risen
items.content: <article>She found a future in the internet’s past with a Tumblr blog of animated texts, a revolt against the clean minimalism of contemporary design aesthetics.</article>

items.title: How Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s Writings Help Explain A.I. Fears
items.author: David Streitfeld
items.content: <article>The collected essays of Dario Amodei help explain why some people are so worried about artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Discloses Six New Incidents of ‘Concerning' A.I. Behavior
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The artificial intelligence company also released a framework for reporting when its systems go wrong.</article>

items.title: Judge Orders Data Sharing and Other Fixes to Solve Google’s Ad Tech Monopoly
items.author: Kate Conger and David McCabe
items.content: <article>The measures, which fall short of a breakup demanded by the government, effectively ensure that the tech titan’s business will continue largely unscathed.</article>

items.title: Merriam-Webster Dictionary Is Wordsmaxxing With 1,400 New Definitions
items.author: Michael Levenson
items.content: <article>Now you have no excuse for not knowing the meaning of “cuffing season,” “shishito” or “glow-up.”</article>

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Takes Aim at Anthropic in Debate Over A.I. Slowdown
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>On social media, Meta’s chief executive appeared to jab at Anthropic by saying that leading A.I. labs should be focused on safety rather than improving their own technology.</article>

items.title: Is There Anything Google’s Fruit Fly Brain Can’t Do?
items.author: Michael Levenson
items.content: <article>Models of the insect’s nervous system have been trained to solve a Rubik’s Cube, play video games and even parallel park a car.</article>

items.title: How to Use AI to Plan a Trip: Better Prompts for Travel Recommendations
items.author: Seth Kugel
items.content: <article>Generic questions get generic answers, experts say, so to avoid mediocre recommendations, you’ll need to write smarter prompts. Follow these tips.</article>

items.title: Age Limits for Social Media Outlined by European Union
items.author: Adam Satariano and Jeanna Smialek
items.content: <article>A proposed law would bar children under 13 from using social media across the 27-nation bloc.</article>

items.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Gets Onstage Call From Trump, Who Dismissed A.I. Safety Concerns
items.author: Kalley Huang, Mike Isaac and Karen Weise
items.content: <article>Mr. Trump called Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, while Mr. Huang was onstage in Los Angeles and criticized calls to slow down and regulate A.I.</article>

items.title: Senate Votes to Block Crypto Bill in Major Blow to the Industry
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany
items.content: <article>The landmark legislation, known as the Clarity Act, stalled in the Senate as Democrats raised concerns about President Trump’s personal investments in crypto.</article>

items.title: Two Chinese Firms Used Binance to Launder Iranian Oil Money, US Says
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany and Michael Forsythe
items.content: <article>Federal prosecutors said proceeds from the sale of Iranian oil flowed through Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, to finance terrorism.</article>

items.title: Gates Foundation Pledges $1 Billion to Combat A.I. Inequality
items.author: Claire Moses
items.content: <article>Bill Gates, the foundation’s chairman, has been vocal about the dangers of artificial intelligence. The donation will be invested in A.I. projects to bridge social inequalities.</article>

items.title: Alex Bores Wants Democrats to Make AI Safety a 2028 Election Issue
items.author: Benjamin Oreskes and Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>Alex Bores, who lost a congressional primary contest that revolved around A.I. regulation, is trying to position himself at the center of the conversation for the next presidential election.</article>

items.title: Amazon Suspends Flights With Airline Whose Plane Crashed in Miami
items.author: Niraj Chokshi
items.content: <article>The online retailer said it would “pause” its relationship with 21 Air, the cargo airline operating a Boeing 767 that overshot a runway in Miami.</article>

items.title: Some in Silicon Valley Are Questioning the Calls for an A.I. Slowdown
items.author: Kalley Huang and Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>The debate over the safety of artificial intelligence grew personal as key tech leaders said calls for government regulation were self-serving and misplaced.</article>

items.title: What Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei Argued in His Call for AI Slowdown
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>Dario Amodei’s 3,800-word letter laid out a three-step plan to rein in artificial intelligence.</article>

items.title: 10-Year-Old Children Predict the Future
items.author: Callie Holtermann
items.content: <article>Robot butlers. Underwater homes. Root beer perfume. Kids across the nation weigh in on what life will be like in the year 2050.</article>
